question: What is the primary purpose of an incident reporting system in a hospital?

options.A: Fulfilling strict legal requirements for patient relatives
options.B: Reducing the overall cost of hospital equipment purchases
options.C: Punishing staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.D: Documenting unexpected occurrences to fix broken processes

explanation: Incident reporting focuses on documenting events to improve system safety rather than punishing staff. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h1)

question: A patient falls out of bed, but suffers no visible injury. Should the nurse report this?

options.A: Yes, because it is an unexpected event that could have caused harm
options.B: No, because the patient did not sustain any visible injury
options.C: Only if the patient or family demands formal documentation
options.D: Only if the doctor specifically notes the fall in the chart

explanation: Incidents include events with potential for harm, even if no actual injury occurred. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h1)

question: An event that almost harms a patient but is caught just in time is called what?
explanation: Near misses are close calls where intervention prevented harm from reaching the patient. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h2)

question: Leaving a surgical instrument inside a patient's abdomen is classified as which type of incident?
explanation: Surgical items left inside patients are shocking errors categorized as never events. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is the main advantage of a blameless reporting culture in nursing?

options.A: Hospital management can easily track down negligent employees
options.B: Staff feel safe reporting errors without fear of harsh punishment
options.C: Doctors take full responsibility for all nursing documentation errors
options.D: Patients receive financial compensation much faster after an injury

explanation: Blameless reporting removes fear, encouraging staff to share mistakes so systems can improve. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h3)

question: Why do punitive hospital cultures often fail to improve patient safety?

options.A: They focus too much on updating clinical guidelines
options.B: They cost too much money to implement in wards
options.C: They encourage too many minor reports from nurses
options.D: They drive staff to hide mistakes out of fear

explanation: Fear of punishment causes healthcare workers to conceal errors rather than report them for analysis. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h3)

question: How should a nurse describe an incident in a formal report?

options.A: Writing speculative guesses about why the event happened
options.B: Blaming the specific colleague who caused the mistake
options.C: Using objective, factual language without personal opinions
options.D: Including emotional words to show deep concern for the patient

explanation: Incident reports require clear, unbiased facts rather than emotional or speculative remarks. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h4)

question: Where should the formal incident report document be stored after completion?

options.A: In the hospital administrative safety database
options.B: Pinned publicly on the ward notice board for review
options.C: Inside the patient's bedside nursing care plan folder
options.D: Inside the patient's permanent clinical case notes

explanation: Incident reports are internal quality documents kept separate from the patient's official clinical chart. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the absolute first action a nurse must take when an incident occurs?

options.A: Sit down to write the detailed incident report form
options.B: Call the hospital security personnel to the ward
options.C: Ensure immediate safety and care for the patient
options.D: Inform the legal department about potential lawsuits

explanation: Patient safety and clinical stabilization always take precedence over paperwork. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why is it important to complete an incident report promptly while memory is fresh?

options.A: To ensure the patient leaves the hospital much earlier
options.B: To give the doctor time to blame the nursing staff
options.C: To avoid paying fines to the nursing council board
options.D: To prevent the loss of accurate details and timelines

explanation: Immediate documentation ensures that critical details and exact timelines are accurately captured. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h5)

question: What is the main goal of performing a Root Cause Analysis after an adverse event?

options.A: Identify underlying system flaws that allowed the error to happen
options.B: Prove that the nursing staff followed all hospital protocols
options.C: Calculate how much financial penalty the hospital must pay
options.D: Find out which individual staff member deserves immediate dismissal

explanation: RCA moves past individual blame to uncover systemic weaknesses in the work environment. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h6)

question: Which factor would a system-level investigation typically examine following a medication error?

options.A: High workload and confusing drug packaging
options.B: How well the patient slept the night before admission
options.C: The personal background and family life of the nurse
options.D: The religious beliefs of the ward manager on duty

explanation: System investigations look at environmental and operational factors like workload and packaging. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h6)

question: Which body regulates professional nursing practice and accountability in Nigeria?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria sets professional standards and accountability rules. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h7)

question: Why must a nurse avoid writing emotional opinions in an incident report?

options.A: Electronic systems automatically delete speculative text
options.B: The report may be used in legal or disciplinary proceedings
options.C: Patients have a right to edit the wording on the form
options.D: Hospital management refuses to read long descriptive paragraphs

explanation: Because reports can be reviewed legally, keeping them factual protects both the nurse and the institution. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h7)

question: What is the final step in making incident reporting truly effective for a hospital?

options.A: Publishing the names of nurses who made errors on social media
options.B: Filing away the paperwork without discussing it on the wards
options.C: Translating report data into practical quality improvement actions
options.D: Locking all completed forms inside the medical director's safe

explanation: Data from reports must be analyzed and used to implement safety improvements. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h8)

question: Why is it important to share lessons learned from incident reviews with all ward staff?

options.A: To prevent similar mistakes from happening across other departments
options.B: To ensure everyone knows who made the original clinical mistake
options.C: To satisfy licensing requirements set by foreign health agencies
options.D: To increase the amount of paperwork nurses must fill daily

explanation: Sharing lessons helps educate the wider team and prevents recurrence throughout the hospital. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h8)
